title: Inflammatory acne
summary: Tracked raised inflammatory features may be compatible with acne; the camera cannot confirm a diagnosis.
mechanisms: Sebum and follicular hyperkeratinisation can block pilosebaceous follicles.
Cutibacterium (formerly Propionibacterium) acnes and immune inflammation contribute to inflamed lesions.
contributing_factors: Occlusive products and repeated friction can worsen susceptible skin.
Androgen sensitivity and genetic predisposition can contribute; hygiene alone does not explain acne.

zone_notes.forehead: Forehead: hair products, fringe occlusion and headwear can contribute to irritation or follicular blockage; location alone does not establish a cause.
zone_notes.nose: Nose: sebaceous gland density is high; visible sebaceous filaments are normal and should not automatically be treated as acne.
zone_notes.left_cheek: Left cheek: phone contact, pillowcase friction and irritating products may contribute; these are possibilities, not a diagnosis.
zone_notes.right_cheek: Right cheek: phone contact, pillowcase friction and irritating products may contribute; these are possibilities, not a diagnosis.
zone_notes.chin: Chin/jawline: follicles can be androgen-sensitive; hormonal influence is possible but cannot be inferred from location alone.
zone_notes.other: Other areas: distribution alone cannot identify a medical cause or an internal organ problem.

see_a_professional: Seek a dermatologist for painful nodules or cysts, scarring, or persistent acne.

ingredient_targets.rationale: Supports the barrier during acne care.

title: Comedonal acne
summary: Tracked plugged-follicle features may resemble blackheads or whiteheads.
mechanisms: Retention of keratin within follicles forms comedones.
Sebum and follicular shedding influence obstruction.
contributing_factors: Occlusive cosmetics and hair products can contribute.
Genetic and androgen-related factors vary between people.

title: Post-inflammatory erythema
summary: Flat red marks can persist after inflammation; they are not necessarily active acne.
mechanisms: Residual superficial vascular changes can follow inflammation.
Barrier irritation can prolong visible redness.
contributing_factors: Picking and friction can sustain inflammation.
UV exposure and over-exfoliation can worsen recovery.

title: Diffuse redness
summary: Broad redness may reflect irritation, flushing or other conditions; lighting affects the estimate.
mechanisms: Vascular dilation can increase visible redness.
An impaired barrier can amplify irritant responses.
contributing_factors: Heat, UV exposure and individual flushing triggers may contribute.
Harsh cleansers or multiple irritating actives may disrupt the barrier.

title: Hyperpigmentation
summary: Uneven darker areas can follow inflammation or sun exposure; a camera cannot distinguish benign spots from concerning lesions.
mechanisms: Inflammation may stimulate excess melanin production.
UV exposure can increase melanin and prolong discoloration.
contributing_factors: Picking or irritating treatments can leave persistent pigment changes.
Sun exposure and hormonal influences may contribute; appearance alone cannot establish the cause.

title: Uneven texture
summary: Camera-estimated surface irregularity may reflect roughness, pores or lighting; it does not measure scars reliably.
mechanisms: Uneven surface shedding can create roughness.
Barrier dryness and follicular features can alter the visible surface.
contributing_factors: Over-cleansing can increase roughness and irritation.
UV exposure and acne history may affect texture.

title: Dehydration and fine lines
summary: Fine lines may be accentuated by surface dryness; the camera cannot establish dehydration or biological age.
mechanisms: Reduced stratum-corneum water can accentuate surface lines.
Natural aging and UV-related changes can also produce lines.
contributing_factors: Dry air and harsh cleansing can increase surface water loss.
A disrupted barrier may reduce moisture retention.

title: Excess sebum
summary: Higher T-zone shine may suggest oiliness; glare, sweat and lighting can produce a similar camera signal.
mechanisms: Sebaceous glands produce lipids under androgen influence.
The T-zone often has greater sebaceous activity than the cheeks.
contributing_factors: Aggressive cleansing can irritate skin without solving sebum production.
